title: Juan Ayuso abandons Paris-Nice after heavy crash, Jonas Vingegaard wins stage and takes yellow jersey
content:
Yellow jersey Juan Ayuso was forced to abandon Paris-Nice after crashing heavily on a rain-soaked stage four, as Jonas Vingegaard delivered a brutal attack in the day’s final kilometre to take the race lead.

The 23-year-old Spaniard, carrying Lidl-Trek’s general classification hopes after leaving UAE Team Emirates before this season, had appeared close to his best form this week.

He entered the day leading by two seconds from INEOS Grenadiers’ Kevin Vauquelin, having targeted the eight-stage Paris-Nice as his main early season goal ahead of July’s Tour de France.

With just under 50km remaining, as part of the lead group making their way through extremely wet conditions, Ayuso was part of a multi-rider fall which also involved UAE Team Emirates’ American climber Brandon McNulty.

After initially remounting his bike, Ayuso quickly had to stop before curling up on the roadside in pain. His abandonment was confirmed moments later and a Lidl-Trek spokesperson later shared that he had been taken to hospital for treatment.

Other crashes also influenced the day’s racing. INEOS pair Vauquelin and Oscar Onley were second and third on GC respectively, but Onley fell while in the front group and steadily lost time despite a huge pull from Josh Tarling, while Vauquelin was dropped earlier on amidst crosswinds.

At the head of the race a leading quartet which included Visma Lease-A-Bike’s Vingegaard, and three Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe riders — Dani Martínez plus twins Tim van Dijke and Mick van Dijke — built a lead of over three minutes.

Mick van Dijke dropped back with six kilometres remaining before Vingegaard launched clear under the flamme rouge. His attack was destructive, gaining 41 seconds over Martinez in just a kilometre, ensuring he would take over Ayuso’s yellow jersey.

Vingegaard’s victory comes almost exactly a year after he crashed out of Paris-Nice last year, suffering a concussion which significantly affected his Tour preparations.

The Dane is now in pole position to win the race — in what would be Visma Lease-a-Bike’s third straight title in this event, his American teammate Matteo Jorgenson having won its past two editions.
